metadata.description: High-priority resource types that, if changed, create immediate security exposure. Covers identity (CA policies, auth methods, cross-tenant access), mail security (anti-phishing, transport rules, DKIM, safe links/attachments), and federation. This is the default profile used by ConvertTo-TCMBaseline and Start-TCMMonitoring.
metadata.quotaNote: ~14 resource types. Fits comfortably within the 200 instances/run quota for most tenants.

controls.title: Conditional Access policies
controls.guidance: CA policies control who can access what and how. Any change to state, grant controls, conditions, or exclusions can open a security gap. TCM monitors all CA policy properties.

controls.title: Authentication method policies
controls.guidance: Controls which MFA methods are enabled, migration state, and per-method configuration. Drift here can weaken MFA posture (e.g., re-enabling SMS).

controls.title: Authorization policies
controls.guidance: Governs app registration permissions, consent framework, guest access, and admin consent workflow. Changes can allow unauthorized app consent or overly permissive guest access.

controls.title: Cross-tenant access policies
controls.guidance: Controls B2B collaboration and direct connect trust with external organizations. Changes to inbound/outbound settings or trusted partners can expose resources to unauthorized tenants.

controls.title: Named location policies
controls.guidance: Named locations define trusted IP ranges and countries used in CA conditions. Adding an IP range or marking a location as trusted can bypass CA policies.

controls.title: Anti-phishing policies and rules
controls.guidance: Controls impersonation protection, mailbox intelligence, spoofing filters. Weakening these policies or changing rule scope exposes users to phishing attacks.

controls.title: Transport rules (mail flow)
controls.guidance: Transport rules can redirect, copy, or modify mail in transit. Unauthorized changes can disable external sender warnings, create hidden forwarding, or strip security headers.

controls.title: DKIM signing configuration
controls.guidance: DKIM signs outbound mail to prevent spoofing. Disabling DKIM or changing signing keys weakens email authentication.

controls.title: Content filter (anti-spam) policies
controls.guidance: Controls spam filtering thresholds, allowed/blocked senders, and IP allow lists. Adding allowed domains or IPs can bypass spam protection entirely.

controls.title: Safe Links policies
controls.guidance: Safe Links rewrites and scans URLs at click time. Disabling or changing scope leaves users vulnerable to malicious links in email and Teams.

controls.title: Safe Attachments policies
controls.guidance: Safe Attachments detonates email attachments in a sandbox. Disabling this or changing the action (e.g., from Block to Monitor) allows malicious payloads through.

controls.title: Teams federation configuration
controls.guidance: Controls which external domains can communicate with your users via Teams/Skype. Opening federation to all domains or allowing unmanaged users enables social engineering attacks.
